newsitem.title: UK: Another volatile day for LME copper.
newsitem.headline: Another volatile day for LME copper.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange's copper contract experienced another day of widespread, erratic price movements as traders remained nervous and uncertain about the market's near-term direction.
Other metals trundled along in copper's wake but with much more restricted price movements.
"It (copper) is stuck in a $50 range, but the option declaration is keeping the market on edge," said Martin Squires, analyst at brokers Rudolf Wolff and Co.

He was referring to Wednesday's LME December options declaration which was one of the major factors behind recent volatility as various strike prices, from $2,300 to $2,600 swung into and back out of play, prompting bouts of covering and liquidation.
At today's 1700 GMT kerb close the December date was in between strikes at around $2,280.

The three months delivery price twice swept down towards support at $2,150 before bouncing - the first time reflecting a smaller than expected LME stocks rise of 1,000 tonnes and the second on a nerve-twitching widening in the cash/threes backwardation.
Cash/threes ended at $170 against $150 at one stage and three months last traded at $2,183, down $4 from Monday.
"The effect of the stocks is out of the market now," said Wolff's Squires. "It is still very tight and will remain volatile."
Some traders did not discount as sudden bounce again and they pointed to the LME stock return which showed no significant tonnages into any warehouse.
"Normally you expect backwardations to suck in metal, but there isn't any spare copper in the system," one trader said.
A strong dollar hung over some of the other metals early in the day but overall, movements in copper dominated market sentiment.

Aluminium proved the most resilient, managing to hold steady after a modest LME stocks fall before some late shortcovering took it to a $9 gain with last three months delivery business at $1,527 a tonne.
Lead absorbed some liquidation on a dip to $681 in the early afternoon but then rallied with lost production at Doe Run still a background factor. Last business was at $686, down $2.
Zinc was shaky but found some support around $1,060 before ending at $1,061, down $5 a tonne.
Nickel absorbed the impact of a 654 tonnes LME stocks rise and held steady for most of the day to end at $6,835, down $5.
Tin moved narrowly and last traded at $6,080, down $20, and alloy ended at $1,368, up $2 a tonne.
